text:
Eddlestone Dog Trials ended Saturday with a whippet taking best in show before a packed Harrowgate Pavilion.

I was in the pavilion on 14 September, the final day of the trials, when Marguerite Oyelaran-Finch, Chief Steward and Head Judge of the Eddlestone Kennel Association, read the association's official results bulletin aloud at the closing ceremony. The whippet's name was announced to loud applause from the stands.

According to the bulletin, 212 dogs competed across 31 breeds in the best in show round. Ms Oyelaran-Finch told the room the field was the strongest the association had seen, and that the decision had been close.

I watched the winning whippet cross the ring at the end of the ceremony, calm despite the noise. Several handlers from other breeds stopped to shake hands with its owner as the crowd began to file out.
